Iran International live, fetched 18:05 BST

Iran’s Army Navy said on Friday that it had detected a tanker on fire east of the Strait of Hormuz, adding that the vessel switched off its tracking systems.

Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian attended the Leaders’ Summit on Biodiversity in Yerevan on Friday, where he greeted Armenian Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan and UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres.

Hassan Hassanzadeh, commander of the Revolutionary Guards’ Mohammad Rasulallah Corps in Tehran, said on Friday that Iran’s adversaries had no option but to accept defeat.

Tehran’s interim Friday prayer Imam praised Iranian forces for targeting three vessels in the Strait of Hormuz after the Tehran-Washington memorandum of understanding, saying the ships had violated a designated route.

In an interview with Newsmax on Thursday, Trump said he would not use nuclear weapons against Iran and had no plans to deploy US ground troops.

Israeli Defense Minister Israel Katz said Israel is pursuing an “offensive, proactive policy” against Iran and nearby threats alongside strengthened border defenses.

Iran would consider Americans, US allies and military bases legitimate targets if Washington used unconventional weapons, including the Mother of All Bombs, deputy chairman of Iran parliament's National Security and Foreign Policy Committee said on Friday.

Abbas Moghtadaei told ICANA, the Iranian parliament's news agency, that using such weapons could turn the White House into the “Black House.”

“If the Americans enter such a situation, all individuals affiliated with the United States, their allies, their overt and covert bases, and every living being of this kind will become legitimate targets for Iran's retaliation,” he said.

He accused Washington of threatening Iran with weapons of nuclear or near-nuclear destructive power and said the threats showed that the United States had exhausted its other options against Iran.

100%Abbas Moghtadaei is an MP from Isfahan and Varzaneh.Oct 16, 2026, 17:13 GMT+1Iran has half the nurses it needs, official saysIran has roughly half the nurses required under national staffing standards, leaving each nurse doing the work of two people, Ahmad Nejatian, head of the Iranian Nursing Organization, said on Friday.

Nejatian said Iran has only about one-third of the regional average number of nurses per patient, describing the shortage as a serious problem for the country's healthcare system. He said the shortage has led to compulsory overtime and increased the number of patients assigned to each nurse, affecting the quality of care.

The warning follows earlier statements by Nejatian that Iran faces a shortage of at least 100,000 nurses, with staffing problems forcing some hospitals to leave wards closed despite having the facilities to operate them.

Fourteen political prisoners in Iran have warned that social media activist Amirhossein Mousavi, known online by the pseudonym James the Godless, could face execution after authorities added charges carrying the death penalty to his case.

The prisoners, in a statement dated Thursday, said Mousavi's charges increased from five to nine following the broadcast of forced confessions on Iranian state television. The new charges include moharebeh, or waging war against God, and efsad fel-arz, or corruption on earth, both punishable by death.

The signatories said the capital charges were absent from his case before the television broadcast and accused security agencies and state media of influencing the judicial process.

Mousavi has been detained since December 2024 and spent approximately six months in solitary confinement before being transferred to a general prison ward. He previously said his televised statements were obtained through beatings, threats against his wife and prolonged isolation.

Iranian cleric Ahmad Alamolhoda welcomed the failure of diplomatic and mediation efforts to end the war with the United States, saying on Friday that they had reached a deadlock.

“Fortunately, all efforts to negotiate with the killers of our martyred leader have failed and produced no results,” Alamolhoda, the Friday prayer leader of Mashhad in northeastern Iran, said, referring to the late supreme leader Ali Khamenei.

He said Iran should resist pressure from the United States and reject concessions, arguing that the country's armed forces had shifted from a defensive to an offensive strategy.

100%Ahmad Alamolhoda is the supreme leader's representative in Razavi Khorasan province and Mashhad's Friday prayer leader. He is also a member of the Assembly of Experts, the clerical body responsible for selecting Iran's supreme leader.Oct 16, 2026, 14:16 GMT+1Iran cleric says Iran-US war should continue until security is assuredIran should continue its war with the United States until it can be confident of lasting security, Yezd’s interim Friday prayer Imam said on Friday.

“The war must continue until we can feel assured,” Nasser Mohammadi said in his sermon. “We want lasting peace and security, and that security must be reliable.”

Mohammadi said negotiations with Washington were meaningless unless it fully abandoned its goals and positions, accusing the United States of speaking of peace while preparing to attack.

He also urged officials to enforce rules against women appearing without mandatory hijab.

German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul said on Friday that Europe is in Iran’s sights, and Germany will not tolerate Iranian hostile activities.

The United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) said on Friday that 12 attacks on vessels were reported over the past week in the Strait of Hormuz, the Persian Gulf and the Gulf of Oman, with one vessel lost.

Ten attacks were reported in the Strait of Hormuz, one in the Persian Gulf and one in the Gulf of Oman, according to UKMTO’s weekly overview. Six vessels continued their voyages or reached port, two were disabled, and the damage or outcome was unconfirmed in three cases.

UKMTO said it was struggling to establish the true number of attacks because most targeted vessels had not reported incidents. It recorded 135 conflict-related maritime incidents since February 28, with 76 people killed or injured.

Combined Strait of Hormuz transits stood at 125 outbound and 129 inbound over the past week, about 70% below pre-conflict levels, the report said.

100%Oct 16, 2026, 13:39 GMT+1Iran envoy says US pressure and ultimatums will not produce resultsIran’s ambassador to Russia said on Friday that continued US use of force and ultimatums would produce no results and would only complicate the region’s situation.

“What can lead the region toward calm is negotiation and honest, transparent and genuine dialogue,” Kazem Jalali said at a meeting in Moscow on Central Asian and Afghan security.

He said Iran remained committed to seeking a lasting agreement through diplomacy but saw no serious willingness to negotiate from the other side.

Jalali also said that more than 33 million Iranians had registered to take part in the country’s defense and were ready to respond to any new attack.

Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian said on Friday that Iran was not seeking nuclear weapons and called claims to the contrary false, during a meeting with Georgia’s prime minister on the sidelines of a biodiversity summit.

“We have always been ready for dialogue. They think they can force us to surrender, but we will not submit to coercion,” he said.

Pezeshkian called US sanctions against Iran and US attacks in recent months unjustifiable and inhumane.
